title: CASE L-22 — the little things
intro: Field Recovery logged an object out of the stacks that does not belong to the System. It is a primer, the kind a child is read from, and every page ends on the same instruction. It came in with its magnifying glass still pressed into the cover. Everything else in the file reads small things in order to itemize someone: a grade, a figure, a sail at the edge of a lookout's glass. This book reads them the other way. Three instruments: what the glass finds in the pictures, the page that shares a word with the house that found the book, and the one tool in the deep stacks that measures the smallest thing the maze is made of.

stations.title: i · the glass
stations.where: a very small book · the pictures
stations.clue: The book has a page of its own now. Its magnifying glass is still in the cover: pick it up. Every picture is hiding one mark, too small to see at the size a page is read — a letter, or only a dot. Carry the glass through the book in page order and read the marks as you go. They make a sentence. File its second word.

link.label: the book — Don’t Forget How Big The Little Things Are

parity: in the record — the book, with its glass
stations.prompt: the second word of the sentence the glass reads — one word
stations.onSolve: a speck. the book hid a whole sentence at the one size nothing in the file is ever counted at. the pictures are not the only place it points — read the words next.

stations.title: ii · the page
stations.where: a very small book · the words
stations.clue: The house that found this book is named for something smaller than a seed, carried on the air, that arises again wherever it lands. One page of the book names that very thing, in the same breath as the smallest monsters there are. Find the page. File its number.

link.label: the book — the words, page by page

parity: in the record — the book, page by page
stations.prompt: the number printed on that page — digits only
stations.onSolve: the house and the book use the same word. nothing in this file was an accident of scale. one instrument left, and it is not in the book. it is at the bottom of the maze.

stations.title: iii · the grain
stations.where: the maze · the deep stacks (levels 2–3) — or the field manual
stations.clue: The maze keeps little things of its own. In the deep stacks, levels 2 and 3, the vending machines carry a tool that is not a provision. It measures the grain, the finest thing the maze is built from, and nothing about it is ever spent. Buy one and look at what it is called, or read what the field manual says the deep machines carry. File the tool.
parity: in the maze — levels 2–3, the vending machines
in the record — the field manual, §06 provisions

maze.hint: you are in the deep stacks. one thing the machines down here sell is a tool, not a provision. /file the last word of its name.

stations.prompt: the tool — the last word of its name, one word
stations.onSolve: the one thing at the bottom of the maze that measures the smallest things. the book said it first: don't forget how big the little things are.

reward.title: the little things are read.
reward.text: Three instruments, and every one of them small: a sentence hidden at the size of a speck, a page that shares a word with the house that found it, a tool that measures the grain. The System counts small things so it can itemize the people they belong to. This book counted them to keep them, and it hid its door at the one scale the ledger has no field for. You found it by looking closer than a page is read.
